body:
## Parent

Part of #23. Found by the CRAN pre-submission sweep for #40.

---

**File / line:** `R/share.R:2600`, `R/share.R:2588`, `R/summary-selections.R:561`

**What is wrong:** Static expression analysis raises untyped base-R errors instead of package conditions at three sites: an `NA`-valued `if()` condition, an unguarded `[[1L]]` on an empty `which()`, and a `vapply(..., character(1))` that a multi-value glue string overflows.

**Reproduction:**

(a) `R/share.R:2600` — `rlang::call_name(expr) %in% c("$", "[[")` yields `logical(0)` for a call whose head is itself a call, so the `&&` chain evaluates to `NA`:

```r
fns <- list(total = function(x, na.rm) sum(x, na.rm = na.rm))
summarize_with_margins(
  retail_sales,
  units = sum(units),
  revenue = fns$total(revenue, TRUE),
  .grouping = rollup(region, store)
)
#> missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed        (class simpleError)
```

The same happens for an inline lambda. Plain dplyr accepts both forms. This is the only one of the 12 `call_name()` sites in `R/` that feeds straight into a condition; its siblings guard with `is.null()` or a NULL-safe `identical()`.

(b) `R/share.R:2588` — `which(arg_names == "")[[1L]]`:

```r
summarize_with_margins(d, tot = sum(units), z = get(mode = "numeric"), .grouping = rollup(g))
#> subscriptOutOfBoundsError
```

dplyr says `argument "x" is missing, with no default`.

(c) `R/summary-selections.R:561` — the `vapply`:

```r
across(c(units), sum, .names = "{c('x','y')}")
#> simpleError: values must be length 1, but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 2
```

dplyr reports a size-compatibility error.

**Notes:** All three violate the condition contract in ADR-0015.

**Severity:** CRAN blocker — crash on legal input.



## Amendments

### 2026-08-07 — acceptance criteria 2 and 3 realigned with ADR-0015

Found during implementation, not triage. The [Agent Brief](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/100#issuecomment-5211553698)'s acceptance criteria are internally
inconsistent: criteria 2 and 3 each demand a `marginplyr_error`, while
criterion 6 forbids converting an External condition into a Package one. Sites
(b) and (c) cannot satisfy both, and ADR-0015 does not treat them alike.

The brief's own instruction — "Verify against plain dplyr what each input
should produce before choosing accept-or-reject" — is what settles it. ADR-0015
makes avoidability the predicate for whether *marginplyr* raises a Package
condition when marginplyr is the one raising. It does not authorise
intercepting a condition someone else raised and reclassifying it; "External
conditions propagate unchanged" is the other half of the same rule.

- **Site (b), `get(mode = "numeric")`.** marginplyr detects nothing here. The
  analysis has no name to read, so it reports no data symbols and the
  expression evaluates; base R's `get()` then raises `missingArgError` against
  the caller's own code. That is an External condition and it propagates. The
  `subscriptOutOfBoundsError` was the defect; a `marginplyr_error` would have
  been a second one.
- **Site (c), the `.names` template.** marginplyr expands the template itself,
  so it knows one column produced two names before anything is staged. Here
  marginplyr is the party raising, the caller avoids it by rewriting the
  template, and ADR-0005 puts the rejection before the query built from it.
  Package condition, as criterion 3 says.

Criteria 2 and 3 in the Agent Brief are superseded by the following. Criteria
1, 4, 5, and 6 stand unchanged.

- [ ] **2 (amended).** A summary expression whose `get()` call names neither
  `x` nor a positional argument evaluates rather than being rejected, and the
  resulting condition reaches the caller with the class and `$parent` base R
  gave it — `identical()` to what plain `dplyr::summarise()` produces for the
  same expression. It must **not** inherit `marginplyr_error`.
- [ ] **3 (amended).** An `across()` `.names` template producing any number of
  names per column other than one — zero as well as more than one — produces a
  `marginplyr_error` naming the template and the column, not a `vapply` type
  error.

### Out of scope, added

Falling through at site (a) exposes a gap the crash had been hiding: the
function position of a call is dropped, so a share read inside a call-valued
head is invisible to the dependency walk. Only the `[[` head — the one shape
whose parts are all data-mask reads — is fixed here. Walking `$` heads or
function-definition heads with the rules this analysis has today rejects calls
dplyr accepts, which is the defect this ticket exists to remove. Tracked as
#130; #100 does not wait for it.

## Blocks

- #40

comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Verification

All three reproduced on `ed6f0c3`, each raising a bare base-R condition with `$parent` of `NULL`:

| Input | Condition class | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `revenue = fns$total(revenue, TRUE)` where `fns` is a list of functions | `simpleError` | `missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed` |
| `z = get(mode = "numeric")` | `subscriptOutOfBoundsError` | `subscript out of bounds` |
| `across(c(units), sum, .names = "{c('x','y')}")` | `simpleError` | `values must be length 1, but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 2` |

Plain dplyr accepts the first input and gives a targeted diagnostic for the other two.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Three sites in the static summary-expression analysis crash with untyped base-R errors on inputs a caller can legitimately write; each must either accept the input or reject it with a package condition.

**Current behavior:**

The analysis that inspects user summary expressions before execution assumes shapes that real expressions do not always have.

1. A test of whether a call is `$` or `[[` compares the call's name against a character vector. For a call whose head is itself a call — which is what `fns$total(x, y)` and an inline lambda produce — the name lookup yields a zero-length value, so the `&&` chain evaluates to `NA` and `if()` stops with "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed". This is the only site among the call-name lookups in the package that feeds a name comparison straight into a condition; the others guard for the null case first.
2. The code that locates the first unnamed argument of a call indexes the result of `which()` with `[[1L]]` without checking that anything matched, so a call with no unnamed argument raises a subscript error.
3. A `vapply()` over generated output names asserts a length-1 character result per element, so a `.names` template that produces more than one value per column overflows the assertion instead of producing a size diagnostic.

**Desired behavior:**

Each of the three inputs produces either a correct result or a `marginplyr_error` that names what the caller must change. Per ADR-0015, an error a caller can avoid by rewriting the call is a Package condition and must be raised as one; an untyped base-R error is neither catchable by class nor actionable.

The first case is the one to be careful with: `fns$total(revenue, TRUE)` and inline lambdas are legal dplyr and should **execute**, not be rejected with a nicer message. The analysis is trying to decide whether an expression is a data-mask reference; a call whose head is a call is simply not one, so the correct outcome is to fall through and let it evaluate normally. Verify against plain dplyr what each input should produce before choosing accept-or-reject.

**Key interfaces:**
- The predicate that classifies an expression as a `$`/`[[` access — must tolerate a call whose head is not a symbol, matching how the package's other call-name lookups guard themselves.
- The helper that finds a call's first unnamed argument — must handle the no-match case.
- The `across()` output-name generation that asserts one name per column — must produce a package condition naming the offending `.names` template when a template yields a different number of names.
- `abort_marginplyr()` and the existing condition vocabulary — reuse; do not introduce a new condition class per site.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `fns$total(...)` where `fns` is a list of functions, and an inline lambda in the same position, both execute and return the result plain dplyr would produce for the equivalent `summarize()`.
- [ ] A summary expression whose call has no unnamed argument produces a `marginplyr_error`, not a subscript error.
- [ ] An `across()` `.names` template producing more than one name per column produces a `marginplyr_error` naming the template, not a `vapply` type error.
- [ ] No input in this issue produces a condition whose class is `simpleError` or `subscriptOutOfBoundsError`.
- [ ] Regression tests cover all three, asserting the condition class and not only the message.
- [ ] Errors that legitimately originate in user code still propagate with their original class and `$parent` intact — this ticket must not convert External conditions into Package conditions (that is the opposite defect, tracked as #107).

**Out of scope:**
- Auditing every other call-name lookup in the package. Only the site that feeds a condition is defective; the others already guard.
- Changing the wording of existing package conditions.

Acceptance criteria 2 and 3 in the Agent Brief above are **superseded**. See `## Amendments` in the issue body.

Short version: the brief's criteria 2 and 3 demand a `marginplyr_error` where criterion 6 forbids one, and sites (b) and (c) fall on opposite sides of that line.

- **(b) `get(mode = "numeric")`** — marginplyr detects nothing; base R raises `missingArgError` against the caller's own code. External condition, propagates unchanged. **Not** a `marginplyr_error`.
- **(c) `.names` template** — marginplyr expands the template itself and knows the names are wrong before staging. Package condition, per ADR-0005.

The brief is left as written, since it is the record of what triage said. The amendment is what the implementation is held to.

title: Static expression analysis raises untyped base-R errors at three sites
